title: The D1 live_round_verdict PASS is fragile and family-dependent
finding: The D1 live_round_verdict PASS rests on a single deciding cell that clears epsilon by 0.0022962496574, and in that same cell the same committed artifact records F_hist_plus at 0.0487633864427 <= epsilon. Under a slightly larger and entirely natural fixed rule family, D1 is bypassable too. The honest reading is therefore that D1's PASS is fragile and family-dependent, not a robust non-bypassability result.
conditionality: The pre-registration fixes min_fixed_r as "min over F, F_size and F_hist of the exact expected normalized regret" and lists F_hist_plus as informational, both before any number existed. F_hist_plus is a 198-cell lookup on DEV-SYN against F_hist's 9, a different complexity class, so excluding it from "cheap fixed rule" is defensible. No committed Gate 0 number is changed by this erratum and no threshold is re-chosen; the D1 verdict stands as recorded, but it stands conditional on the pre-registered family set {F, F_size, F_hist}.
structural_reading: A gate stops looking bypassed only until a cheap legal strategy is admitted into the comparison set. That is the same failure mode the repository already recorded for the four-cell W4 design, where always_restage bypassed S in every cell because free recomputation was available (faultda_bench/docs/FOUR_CELL_WITNESS_2026_10_18.md). It recurring at the D1 stage, after the rev-1 map was already reported as bypassable, is evidence that the bypass is structural to this environment rather than an artifact of one parameterisation.

rev1_headline_unaffected.note: The headline rev-1 result is hard_stop true with or without F_hist_plus.

claim_decision_consequence: The final review identifies the D1 PASS as the last un-falsified support for research claim A. With this disclosure that support is materially weakened. It does not by itself decide between claim A and claim B; the decision remains the owner's and is made in no document of this version.
recorded_outside_the_amendments_array: This erratum is recorded in its own file and in RELEASE_0565.md and CLAIM_DECISION_INPUT_0565.md rather than appended to faultda_bench/protocols/vericost_v1_amendments.json, because that file's sha256 is pinned as inputs.amendments inside the write-once analysis.json, which audit --cross-version regenerates and compares byte for byte against the committed copy. Appending would flip matches_committed to false and break the cross-interpreter byte-identity proof, and analysis.json cannot absorb the new hash because it is a pre-registered write-once output. The pre-registered mechanism for exactly this case is analysis_erratum<k>.json (prereg amendment_policy.timing), which is what this file is. The deviation is documented rather than silent.

gate0.d1.dev_syn.live_round_verdict.read: PASS: a usable configuration for a future live round

PASS, conditional on the pre-registered family set {F, F_size, F_hist}; the deciding cell clears epsilon by 0.0022962496574 and F_hist_plus attains 0.0487633864427 <= epsilon in that same cell, so D1 is bypassable under a slightly larger fixed family and the verdict is fragile and family-dependent
